units.translation: and does not pity the suffering
about to see this suffering of bondage
of a hymn to the dead
Paean is said of Apollo himself as deliverer

as Hartung (except that he wrote παιῶνα [paean]) for αἰῶνα [lifetime]. (Thus Pherecrates in Athenaeus 15 p. 685a: ἔγχει κἀπιβόα τρίτον παιῶν, ὡς νόμος ἐστίν [pour and call for the third paean, as is the custom].)
Thus Blomfield correctly for παιών [paean], whom see on Sept. 254: these are often interchanged, about which I have spoken in Thes. vol. 6 p. 58.

where the scholiast: ὅτι ἐπὶ θανόντος εἶπε κακῶς · καὶ (εἶπὲν ὡς καὶ [that he spoke ill of the dead; and (he said as also] Blomfield) Εὐριπίδης [Euripides] (Alc. 424) “παιῶνα τῷ κάτωθεν ἀσπόνδῳ θεῷ” [a paean to the god below with whom there is no truce]
where I corrected ἰήιον δ᾽ ἐπανακαλῶ Παιᾶν᾽, ἰή [I call upon the healer, Paean, ie]. See Thes. vol. 6 p. 25.

it is fitting to call this a paean of the Erinyes

O Death, healer, do not dishonor me by not coming. For you alone are the healer of incurable evils.

χόλον Μ [anger M], which Doederlein corrected
so that the present crowd of toils seems to you to be play
who is so childish or struck in his wits?
this strife that destroys children urges on
I corrected the faulty accent in M, παιδολύμας [child-destroying]. A similar form of adjective is ἐρικυμάδα [wave-swelling], which Seidler restored at Ag. 119 for ἐρικύματα [waves].
the wretched son-destroying daughter of Thestius
many true child-wounding sufferings await the parents
In the plural παῖδες [children] means children.
Thus I corrected for ἐμῷ παιδί [my child].
Are you not a child and even more foolish than this?
you mocked me as if I were a child
